messages:
Kaitlyn (CS): @Maya @Jonah Customer LambdaHealth says their last three invoices include burst charges that should have been covered by reserved capacity pro‑rata. They sent a CSV and invoice links: https://invoices/redwood/INV-4982
Maya (Finance): Can you paste the CSV sample lines and the invoice line items? I need a quick scope estimate before we touch billing.
Kaitlyn (CS): CSV snippet they sent:

"ts","meter_type","tokens","billable","note"
"2027-04-12T10:14:03Z","generation","480","true","burst_applied_during_partial_hour"
"2027-04-12T10:28:17Z","generation","640","true","burst_applied_during_partial_hour"

Invoice shows 2x burst lines for 2027-04-12, total $12.80.

Jonah (Billing Eng): Hypothesis: we applied burst pricing for the whole hour because reserved capacity state flipped at 10:00 but our apportionment code uses hour buckets. I'll validate with a query.

Jonah (Billing Eng): Quick query I'm running (ClickHouse):

```
SELECT customer_id, toStartOfHour(ts) as h, sum(tokens) as tokens, any(burst_applied) as burst
FROM usage_events
WHERE customer_id = 'lambda' AND ts BETWEEN '2027-04-12 09:00:00' AND '2027-04-12 11:00:00'
GROUP BY customer_id, h
ORDER BY h;
```

Jonah (Billing Eng): Dry-run output shows hour 10:00 has burst=true and tokens=1120, but reserved_capacity switched at 10:20 which should have pro‑rated out 60% of the hour. So 60% of tokens should be billed at reserved rate, 40% as burst — we incorrectly billed 100% as burst.

Kaitlyn (CS): Customer says they scaled down at 10:20 and expected prorated pricing. They provided API timestamps matching Jonah's findings.

Jonah (Billing Eng): I'll run the backfill dry-run now to compute correct deltas.

metering-bot: backfill:dryrun started for customer=lambda start=2027-04-12T09:00 end=2027-04-12T11:00 job_id=bfr-20270412-01

Jonah (Billing Eng): Running command:

```
python tools/backfill_metering.py \
  --customer lambda \
  --start '2027-04-12T09:00:00Z' \
  --end '2027-04-12T11:00:00Z' \
  --policy prorate-on-capacity-change \
  --dry-run
```

metering-bot: dry-run complete — proposed credit: $8.64 (down from billed $12.80). Affected invoices: INV-4982 (partial), INV-4983 (same window). Details saved to gs://redwood-metering/backfills/dryruns/bfr-20270412-01.json

Maya (Finance): Good to see a number. Approve issuing the $8.64 credit if the dry-run matches repo. Two asks: (1) include a brief note for the customer explaining proration, (2) add a unit test for the apportionment logic.

Jonah (Billing Eng): Agreed. I'll re-run without --dry-run once I get thumbs-up. Estimate runtime ~2m. I'll also open a PR with the unit test.

Kaitlyn (CS): I'll draft the customer email and include that we will apply the credit to INV-4983 and issue a small courtesy credit on INV-4982. Will wait for final confirmation before sending.

Maya (Finance): Approved — proceed with production backfill and issue credit. Please tag me in the PR and paste the final backfill output here.

Jonah (Billing Eng): Running production now.

metering-bot: backfill:run succeeded job_id=bfr-20270412-01 reprocessed_tokens=1120 adjusted_credit=8.64 artifacts=gs://redwood-metering/backfills/bfr-20270412-01.json

Jonah (Billing Eng): Done. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/542 includes unit test and the apportionment fix. Backfill output attached to artifact. Billing adjustments queued; invoice credits will be applied in next billing cycle.

Kaitlyn (CS): Sending customer note now. Thanks team. :tada:

Maya (Finance): Marking this as resolved. Follow-ups: add perf test for large windows; run a sweep for customers that had capacity changes in the last 30 days.

Jonah (Billing Eng): I'll add the sweep to next week's job; opening issue #1187.

Kaitlyn (CS): Closing loop with customer once credit posts.
